issue: Is a district court order disentitling a foreign citizen who remains abroad from seeking relief in his pending federal criminal case immediately appealable under the collateral order doctrine?

sides.position: A fugitive disentitlement order against a foreign citizen who remains abroad is immediately appealable under the collateral order doctrine.
cases: United States v. Sindzingre, No. 19-1698 (2d Cir. 2022)

sides.position: Fugitive disentitlement orders are not immediately appealable, including where the order concerns a foreign citizen located abroad.
cases: United States v. Martirossian, 917 F.3d (9th Cir.) (cited at 887; circuit not stated in excerpt)
United States v. Shalhoub, 855 F.3d 1255 (11th Cir. 2017)

this_court: Immediately appealable: the majority holds the court has jurisdiction to review such an order. The dissent, which identifies the split, argues the court should instead conclude it lacks appellate jurisdiction.
quote: In doing so, it creates a split with our sister circuits who have held that fugitive disentitlement orders—including those specifically involving, as here, a foreign citizen located abroad—are not immediately appealable.
cite: United States v. Sindzingre, No. 19-1698 (2d Cir. 2022)
